title: The Spirit in Scripture
english: He wrote to Timothy: 'For God did not give you a spirit of slavery, but a spirit of power and love and self-control' (2 Timothy 1:7), and to the Romans: 'I urge you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit' (Romans 15:30), and to the Galatians: 'But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace' (Galatians 5:22), similar to 'God is love' (1 John 4:8), and to 'He transferred [us] into the kingdom of the love of his Son' (Revelation 22:2); and 'just as Christ loved the church' (Ephesians 5:2), and again: 'the Son of God who loved me' (Galatians 2:20), similar also to 'you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the power of the Father' (Mark 13:32), and to 'I knew a power going out from me' (John 10:40).

A spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and strength, a spirit of knowledge and godliness; a spirit of the fear of God, a spirit of judgment and burning, as Isaiah prophesies; and as Wisdom says: 'for the spirit of wisdom is a lover of mankind,' and as Moses relates in Exodus: 'Behold, God has called by name Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and has filled him with a divine spirit of wisdom and understanding and knowledge' (Exodus 31:2), and according to Baruch: 'You have left the fountain of wisdom' (Baruch 3:9), and as the proverbs teach: 'God established the earth by wisdom, and prepared the heavens by understanding' (Proverbs 3:19), just as Isaiah said concerning God the Father: 'He was wise in doing evil against them' (Isaiah 5:5). And concerning the Only-Begotten, Paul said: 'Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God' (1 Corinthians 1:24); and another: 'I will bless the Lord who gave me understanding' (Psalm 119:34).

A spirit of gentleness, just as Paul admonishes the Galatians: 'Brothers, if even a person is caught in a transgression, you who are spiritual should restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness' (Galatians 6:1). A spirit of discipline, that is, of wisdom. For wisdom says: 'the spirit of discipline will flee from guile, and will turn away from foolish thoughts.' A spirit of adoption, as—

Paul first sent to the Romans: 'For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God' (Rom 8:14). 'For you received the Spirit of adoption, in whom we cry: Abba, Father; the Spirit itself bears witness with our spirit, that we are children of God' (Rom 8:15-16).

3.12 The Spirit of promise, according to the same apostle writing to the Ephesians: 'in whom also, having believed, you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is the pledge of our inheritance' (Eph 1:13), and to the Galatians: 'Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us. For it is written: Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree; so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith' (Gal 3:13-14).

3.13 The Spirit of faith and revelation, according to the same [apostle] to the Corinthians: declaring in the second epistle: 'having the same Spirit of faith' (2 Cor 3:3), and again: 'but God revealed to us through His Spirit' (1 Cor 2:10). This is similar to what he showed to the Romans: 'God is faithful, through whom you were called into the fellowship of His Son' (1 Cor 1:9), and to that which was said under Moses in Deuteronomy: 'and you shall know today, that the Lord your God, He is God, the faithful God' (Deut 7:9), and to the Psalmist: 'Faithful is the Lord in all His words and holy in all His works' (Ps 119:89, 160).

3.14 The guiding Spirit, the straight Spirit, according to David in the 4th [Psalm] confessing: 'With a guiding spirit, sustain me' (Ps 143:10); likewise to the Psalmist in the 122nd [Psalm]: 'For straight is the word of the Lord, and all His works are in faithfulness' (Ps 33:4), and to Moses saying: 'Straight is the Lord our God, and there is no injustice in Him' (Deut 32:4).

3.15 The Spirit of grace, just as the apostle writes to the Hebrews: 'He who has despised the Son of God and insulted the Spirit of grace' (Heb 10:29); for the same one also wrote concerning the Father: 'I am by the grace of God, as I am' (1 Cor 15:10), and his grace is in me; and concerning the Son: 'The grace of our Lord Jesus...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
